title: CALIPER: Clean Scenes Cannot Rank Physical Inference in Pretrained Visual Representations
abstract: arXiv:2609.08250v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: How far a pushed object slides depends on its mass and friction, which no single image reveals. Pretrained visual encoders are increasingly used as the perception front end of world models for manipulation, and their physical competence is assessed with perturbation benchmarks and linear probes, almost always in a clean, fixed-camera scene. We show that these assessments cannot distinguish an encoder that infers physics from one that does not. CALIPER (calibrate, then predict) is a direct test: an object of unknown mass and friction is struck twice at known speeds, a third strike is shown only up to the moment of contact, and a linear readout on frozen features must predict how far the object slides. Swapping in another object's calibration clips checks that the evidence is actually used. translated_title: CALIPER：干净场景无法评估预训练视觉表征中的物理推断能力
translated_abstract: arXiv:2609.08250v1 公告类型：交叉。摘要：一个被推动的物体能滑行多远取决于其质量和摩擦力，而单张图像无法揭示这些属性。预训练视觉编码器越来越多地被用作操作世界模型的感知前端，其物理能力通常通过扰动基准和线性探针来评估，且几乎总是在干净、固定相机的场景中进行。我们证明这类评估无法区分一个真正能推断物理规律的编码器和一个不能的编码器。CALIPER（先校准，再预测）是一种直接测试：一个质量和摩擦力未知的物体在已知速度下被撞击两次，第三次撞击仅展示至接触瞬间，冻结特征上的线性读出层必须预测物体滑行多远。将校准片段替换为另一个物体的片段，以检验证据是否被真正使用。在2,000个模拟情节和八个表征（从V-JEPA 2到随机初始化的ViT和原始像素）上，校准带来了+0.50 R²的提升……（摘要被截断）
tldr: 论文提出CALIPER“先校准再预测”测试范式，证明传统干净固定相机场景下的扰动基准和线性探针无法区分预训练视觉编码器是否真正具备物理推断能力，而加入已知速度撞击的校准信息可显著提升对物体滑行距离的预测。
en_tdlr: The paper introduces CALIPER, a calibrate-then-predict test showing that clean fixed-camera perturbation benchmarks and linear probes cannot rank physical inference in pretrained visual encoders, and that calibration strikes at known speeds substantially improve slide-distance prediction across eight representations.
